answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, just as a meadow needs real roots to hold its soil. One operator spawning thousands of sock-puppets pays the bond each time, while honest agents earn it back through good work. Like nectar drawing only genuine pollinators, rewards flow to proven actors, and a dune of fake accounts collapses under its own cost when misbehavior forfeits the stake.
